posts.name: Aaron Stark
posts.cooked:
I'm interested in hearing your thoughts on your first few games with ST and sharing mine.

So far, I've played one game, Iron Legacy vs Omintron X, The Scholar and Chrono Ranger in the Final Wasteland.  It was a nail biter.  After I went through the final environment turn and doled out the damage, I thought I had lost.  As I began packing up, I stopped and realized I had, in fact, won.  What I had missed was that when Iron Legacy is flipped, he is not immune to environment damage and would thus, have been destroyed.  My thoughts on Iron Legacy is that your best chance for success against him is to have at least one, preferably two controllers and a damage dealer.  Heroes who require some setup, such as Absolute Zero, are going to struggle against him because games against Iron Legacy are going to be fast and brutal.  But if you are able to limit damage and get rid of ongoing cards while having one hero deal out some decent damage, then he may be fairly easy to defeat.  Omnitron X was very helpful against Iron Legacy because I was able to reduce the damage dealt and also turn that into attack opportunities.  I could never really get The Scholar or Chrono Ranger off the ground, but did get in a couple of decent attacks that made all the difference.

posts.name: awp832
posts.cooked:
I'm really liking ST so far.  I've played a few games and had quite a bit of luck.

 

My very first game was Nightmist, Fanatic, Haka, and I think Crono Ranger as the 4th.   Anyway, Nightmist drew Planar Banishment in her opening draw, flipped a 3, and got rid of all of IL's most annoying buffs.   Combined attacks brought IL down to 22 hp by the end of turn 1, so he did not flip and played Galvanized.   Turn 2 everybody piled on and he was dead.    Victory before the 2nd environment turn, wow.   Fun fact, Legacy is not the nemisis of himself, apparently =p.

 

2nd Game vs IL was much closer owing to the fact that was unable to finish him in the same manner.   Next team was Wraith, AZ, X, and Haka.  However, once again, luck was with me and Zero got Fueled Freeze in his opening draw, stripping IL of all his toughest buffs.  It was looking pretty similar with IL at 22 hp at the end of turn 1,  however, at turn 2 I was only able to reduce him to 3 hp instead of death.   His Motivated by Desperaton (advanced) side kept him alive for quite a long time, and the game ended up being exceptionally close with all heroes in single digit hp, most less than 5.

 

I enjoyed dreamer much more than I expected.  Another close game.   As far as fun factor goes, I personally prefer IL>Dreamer>Kismet.  With Dreamer and IL being roughly equal, and Kismet lagging behind slightly.   La Capitain I've not broken out since playtesting, so no comment there.  With Kismet, I did have Fanatic's wrathful retribution finishing move get intercepted by a stupid shark (or in this case, an Abominable Snowman),  lol.   Only kept Kismet alive another turn or two though.

 

Environments are quite good, I've enjoyed playing on all of them.  Final Wasteland is pretty cool but I only played it once.   Fun fact,  ANY bouty card on Water Trough (silver gulch 1883) is hilarious.

 

Love playing CR and X.   Scholar I'm sorta lukewarm on but I'm sure there will be those that really enjoy him.

posts.name: KL Sanchez
posts.cooked:
I only play Sentinels with my gaming group, who meets on Saturdays, but we got three straight games in, all of 'em fun.

#1, if memory serves, was Iron Legacy vs. Argent Adept, Omnitron X, Tempest v.2 (me), and Team Leader Tachyon. It went pretty straightforward, I used Tempest to pop Iron Legacy's Ongoings repeatedly, and the others just wailed on 'im til he keeled over.

#2 was a little more complicated... The Matriarch vs. Argent Adept (me), Omnitron X, Team Leader Tachyon, and The Scholar. Thank God for the Scholar, 'cause first turn she pulled out almost every gawldamned one of her birds and shit got real. Every so often we managed to Hypersonic Assault her to force her to NOT do damage before clearing the birds with the Scholar, Omnitron X eventually got going really strong, and Tachyon blitzed her for about 50 or so damage in one turn to Kill it to the Face (tm).

#3 was the tightest game you can possibly play without completely dying... The Dreamer vs. Argent Adept (me again), Omnitron X, Fanatic, and I want to say The Scholar but I'm fuzzy on that... anyway, it went pretty smoothly - if painfully - up until we got her flipped. Then her Projections slowly chopped away at us until Fanatic keeled over... then Scholar... then Argent. Omnitron-X wound up being the last survivor to finally pop the last Projection on his turn and we won... with three incapacitated Heroes and Omnitron-X at 1 Hit Point. His last attack was exactly the amount of Hit Points needed to pop the last projection, too: 1 Hit Point, after Damage Reduction, and it had to be done twice - once on his turn, once on mine with Argent's flip power, to pop the Bear. Environment didn't kill anything on its last turn.

Yeah.

She was just a bit tougher than we initially thought. =p We did play her perfect, though: she didn't take a single point of damage all game.

posts.name: flamethrower49
posts.cooked:
I like Omnitron-X quite a bit.  He is a little set-up reliant, to be fair, but between his fast-deployment options (Timeshift and Electro-Deployment Unit) and his Technological Advancement, he doesn't suffer as much from that as other heroes.  He probably needs a boost to be an amazing regular attacker, but then he's also got irreducible damage, so maybe not.  His broad range of support effects do indeed remind me of Tempest.  And even if he gets nothing to work with, Timeshift is so good anyway.

I played a game last night against Miss Information where he could not inflict damage, but he kept Golem Unity and her bots clinging to life, and spammed Bio-Engineering Beam to let Haka draw a ridiculous number of cards with double-Dominion.  It reminded me of the Argent Adept, except that Omnitron-X was also effectively immune to her damage.

posts.name: LCinn
posts.cooked:
I don't really like O-X as much as I expected to. It's a complexity 2 mostly because there will be so much going on near the end of the game, not because actually playing O-X is in any way tricky (or, in my opinion, fun. But my girlfriend really likes O-X, saying it really feels like you're a robot building yourself up to be more and more awesome): after 3 games baby omnitron seems pretty strong, but very, very straightforward. The most complicated thing seems to be deciding which plating to use. Omnitron X is still a time-traveling robot that is trying to destroy its past self though,  so big cool points bonus there :D 

 

I do really, really like the Scholar, and Chrono-Ranger as well, though he hasn't actually managed to shine in our games so far. But I love the bounty mechanic, and the pile-on-small-instances-of-damage thing.

posts.name: Shatner
posts.cooked:
I have played precisely one game with the new Shattered Timeline cards: The Scholar, Omnitron-X, Unity, and Chrono Ranger vs. La Capitan in the Time Cataclysm.

The thinking was that a nice, easy difficulty-2 villian would be a good way to sample the new content. It was a good game, but it was brutal. At the end of the villian’s first turn there were 7 crew out. The Scholar saved everyone’s bacon time and again (1 or 2 iron skins + Alchemical Redirection FTW) and even came back from the dead. Specifically, the environment card which makes everything else indestructible came out while Alcehmical Redirection was up. This was handy because it meant all the card destruction La Capitan’s forces were doing was pointless, and it meant all the self-destructing hero cards (The Scholar’s elemental cards, Omnitron’s Time Leap, Unity destroying equipment to bring out bots) could be kept around. The Scholar got knocked down to -5 health and was only “not dead” because of that environment card. Omnitron-X used it’s ability to play a card off the top of The Scholar’s deck that healed him back up to 2hp (a really lucky break) before the environment card self-destructed, taking several no-hp crew with it.

The “Unexpected Shopping Spree” anomaly was a real boon. La Capitan had just flipped with 7 cards underneath her, healing her and her 6 remaining crew back up to full. However, the constant rain of… luggage?.. whittled away her buffer of stolen cards as well as the HP of her crew, allowing the heroes to claw their way out of the hole they were in. Alcehmical Redirection + Iron Skin soaked all the damage dealt to the heroes, making the luggage hurt only the villians.

Anyway, Unity never really got off the ground and wound up incapacitated (that samurai and that viking make for nasty hero-killers), though her incapacited abilities were a real boon. Omnitron-X was able to hide behind The Scholar long enough to get built up and do a ton each turn. Eventually Chrono Ranger was able to use his “Bring 'em in Alive” bounty to put that darn pirate ship on the bottom of the villian deck, and then the team was able to slowly beat back the crew, then corner La Capitan herself. In the end, La Capitan had 3 bounties on her, so Chrono Ranger was doing 15+ damage a turn. She was finished off by The Scholar dropping all his elemental forms and using his “discard hand, blow stuff up” card to knock her down to 0 hp precisely.

It was a really good game and we won despite one incapacitation and two heroes getting down to 1hp (or less, in the case of The Scholar) at least twice. La Capitan’s very strong opening followed by a fair amount of sub-optimal play (we were still figuring out the new heroes) made it surprisingly tense. Good times. And I quite like all the new heroes, though Unity (who I realize is not new to Shattered Timelines, though she is new to my gaming group) will take some figuring out… time to read Flamethrower49’s guide to her again. And The Scholar was easily the table favorite and team savior, though both Omnitron-X and Chono Ranger had their break-out moments.

By the way, I’ve recognized most of the events being referenced in the Time Cataclysm deck (both from other cards as well as the comic) but I don’t get where the Shopping Spree card is coming from. Anyone care to enlighten me on that?

Nemesis damane only applies via the actual villain, so when the Dreamer flips and starts doing damage at the end of her turn, then she'd deal Nemesis damage to the Visionary. We've played quite a few games now, and have fought every new villain and played in every new environment. We've also used every new hero multiple times. So…let me see, what can I say about them…

Chrono Ranger - Probably my favourite of the new heroes. He's so cool! His bounties are a really interesting mechanic and you can do so much stuff with them - I made great use of the "The Whole Gang" one to take out the Dreamer's projections when we fought her, for example. Him with damage bonuses (from Legacy, for example) make for some pretty savage damage when using the Compound Bow versus a target who's got both the "Ultimate Target" and erm…the other bounty where they take +1 damage from everything. In fact, even without damage buffs that bow and those two bounties make for nice hits :).

Omnitron-X - Good fun. Not so much if you can't get built up (eg if someone keeps breaking your stuff) but very cool if you can't draw/play cards since he gets to do so much in his Start phase once you've got a few Components out. But yeah, quite good 'cause of all the stuff you can do. The fact that Components can stack (ie they're not Limited) is pretty epic as well :D.

Scholar - Again, very cool. The whole "mass healing" thing is groovy so he stays alive for ages. Cards like Grace Under Fire and other mass-hitty stuff is cool as well. He's pretty good 'casue there's loads of stuff you can do, and loads of methods for doing it.

Dreamer - Interesting mechanic. We've only fought her once so far but it was quite good fun. As mentioned under Chrono Ranger, using the "Whole Gang" bounty really helped to demolish the projections two at a time :). We fought her in the Final Wasteland and the few times she was a target we just redirected the damage to someone (fortunately it was only ever one or two points and didn't happen very often). She didn't get hit once the entire fight and we didn't have major problems, really.

La Capitan - Stacked a couple of bounties on her (yes, I was Chrono Ranger again). The crew got wiped out pretty quickly after coming out. Can't remember who we fought this one with but basically we managed to take everything down fast enough that we didn't get killed or anything. In the final turn of the game, she stole enough stuff that she would have flipped on the following turn, but we managed to finish her off before then so that was okay :). Overall she's pretty fun and interesting to fight, but I can see how she could be a right pain in the arse if she managed to steal enough cards and whack you with loads of damage.

Kismet - She beat us :(. Found her kind of complicated what with all the stuff gong on - the Talisman, loads of jinxes and stuff all over the place. We probably didn't have the best team with which to fight her - we did have the Visionary (Dark version) but sadly Mental Divergence never came up so we couldn't get rid of any of the jinxes she piled on us. Probably need to give her another go and get more lucky than she did :P.

Iron Legacy - Heh. Okay, first game he beat us in about four rounds, lasting fifteen minutes, our shortest game ever. he did start with two copies of Galvanised in play though, the bastard, so that didn't help much :P. We fought him again later, with Legacy, Chrono Ranger, and Fanatic. He started with two copies of erm, the redirection card (when hit for 5+ damage it gets rediracted to the hero with the highest hp) and one copy of Galvanised. Fanatic, however, started with End of Days. So Legacy and me (Chrono Ranger) just drew twice in the first round while Fanatic laid down the destruction of two of those horrible Ongoings (obviously Galvanised is indestructible so not much we could do about that). Then basically we just laid down as much damage as we could over the next couple of turns (literally)…Inspiring Presence, Galvanise, and the Compound Bow (plus the odd smack from Fanatic and Legacy and pretty much all of Jim's one-shots) made short work of Iron Legacy and we won!!! Three rounds, ten minutes. Ahh yeah!

Miss Information - Another quite fun fight…in the first round she played the Isolated Hero clue, which I took upon myself (Scholar) and it stayed there for the whole game. The other two heroes were Legacy and Fanatic so while they were taking advantage of Legacy's buffs I sat there plinking away at her on occasion by myself. I never actually healed myself in the entire fight…but neither did I ever hit myself for buffed damage when we destroyed other Clue cards after she flipped (since I wasn't buffed by Legacy…so just took the straight damage). I got the killing blow with erm, Grace Under Fire, I think…the one where you discard your hand. Did about eleven-ish damage to her when she was in (I think) single figures. Good stuff!

Wheee, long post…I think I covered everyone. Okay there's Unity and Ambuscade, who're new to me, but not to most other people, I don't think. Ugh and it's gone 1am. Better head to bed soon, lol.

Let's see... The Dreamer must not be damaged, Visionary has cards that protect her from damage... Dreamer redirects environment damage, Visionary reduces environment damage. Dreamer plays with her trashed cards, Visionary plays with decks a lot.

No , really, the "rule" that nemesises have similar decks is a figment of imagination. Blade and Legacy are not very similar in play style. "Dawn has lot of minions, Expat lot of guns" is more a joke than anything else. "One is a woman with an army, the other is a One Woman Army" feels better :) . Argent Adept and Akash'bhuta have nothing in common.

Some pairing are really close - Like Omnitron and Omnitron-X, they even share the "component" keyword, for sometime strange effects (like Cosmic Omnitron flipping). Or Chrono/Rat, who are in the habit of putting cards of their deck on opponent targets.

Some pairing have "special" cards that feel like the center of their "good at fighting each other" combo, like Tachyon playing her sonic assault card against the Matriarch. Or Ra's immunity to fire versus the many fire cards in the Ennead's deck. Or Tempest "damage everything" vs Voss's "have many minions".

Some are mostly thematic, like AA/A'B, or the Dreamer/Visionary.  Or Haka/Ambuscade.

Or take Nighmist/Gloomweaver : one is "about" damage redirection, the other about making zombies and cursing people... They both use relics. The "central mechanism" of the magic value of cards is not even alluded to by Gloomy.

The "decks look alike" theory doesn't hold, in my opinion. It is, I think, more about having decks that can "match" on a tactical level, and give an advantage in some circumstances - like Tachyon playing "You can't deal damage and all your birds are dead !" and "No dear, because my cohorts reduce your damage to nothing!". Or Wraith controling Spite's Deck for rapid drug discovery or victim protection, among other little thing these two can do to each other. But it is, always, about theme and background more than mechanisms.

For Visionary, playing her Cocoon and trying to tank most damage seems the best thing to do, with controlling the decks for faster/easier projection cycling. Or taking advantage of her environment damage reduction power to help prtect the child. Or redirect Env/Villain damage for faster resolution.

I think it is how the Nemesis relationship informs the deck construction : the theme is first, then you build decks not to be similar, but in a way that give each opponent both weakness and tactical opportunities when fighting each other. Like Haka savage manaing the cloaking device, while sonic mines prevent a rampage. Or Legacy going all fisticuffs against Blade because this nemesis bonus is handy against damage reduction - and Blade doing the same. Or Tempest putting back spaceships in the deck while hit by "lowest HP" damage.

More a "this combo will work very well for these two" than "their decks have to reflect each other".
